steps.content: (Previously experienced scenes from 3D world, white transition montage)
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: It's over...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I only know how to control Nightmare, and I've been searching for Mania power in this dream to call it out.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Fortunately, all my attempts have failed in this world.
She looks back at the apparitions in the dream. The two worlds are churning, and the blurry figures are gradually fading away...

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I have to go back to my Chief now. Thank you all. May this always be a beautiful dream.
The system reluctantly emits a final beep. You press a random button, activating the permissions. As everyone had hoped, it shuts up.
This is the victory you all strived hard for. You feel a lot of satisfaction in your heart. This is the joy of winning a game.
You gave up your place as the main character and became a system error like me... Didn't expect you to be this reckless live wire.
You really want me to come back that much?

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Yeah, I risked my life to save you.
Nah, it's because I'm the MBCC Chief.

steps.content: She laughs happily, hugging your arm a little tighter.
Oh shucks, I'm blushing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Blushing? I thought all of this was part of your plan.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You put so much thought into me. Since you wanted me to "save" you this much, of course I had to come.
Alright, alright. I won't come to your Bureau ever again, then. Don't regret it!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Really? Won't you find all sorts of backdoors to sneak into my Bureau?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You used so many tricks along the way, and finally got me where you wanted.
Hmm... good point. That is something I would do.
So... you took the bait? You're not the kind of person who would act so dashingly out of character for me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "You're this kind of person, not that kind of person..." You always say things like that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For someone who hates having others script your story, you sure love to give me labels.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't say you know me well. We've only known each other for a few days. You don't know that much.
You pat her cat ears.
Is that so? But there's one thing I do know. Don't try to guess a girl's heart, Chief.
Is it possible that I cling to you simply because I like you and want to be with you for a little while?
How should you answer her? You remember the most important information the system gave you.

<color=#cafffc>The error correction system only corrects internal system errors.
We do not handle external anomalies.</color>

<color=#cafffc>Moreover, Mania would never appear in the real world, nor would there be mysterious forces to stop Mania.
Because Mania is purely fictional.</color>
You guys defeated the powerful game correction system, but things aren't over yet. The powerful enemy that has been blocking Mania and destroying 000 hasn't arrived yet.
It's some rule that's of a higher dimension than anything in this world. The permissions are powerless before it.

Its function is probably to uphold order, ensuring that the duck gods here will never discover Mania or have erroneous delusions. It ensures that in this world, fiction and imagination can never distort reality.
So, when the ducks wake up from the nightmare and find the system has been tampered with, your game should end.

Even if you want to stay, there are more important things at hand. You take her hand and share all the gods' permissions. Leaving decisively is the best solution right now. You prepare your farewell words.
But she grasps your hand and floats up, lifting your face.
This time, she doesn't bump your lips. She just gets close and gently presses her forehead against yours.
Thank you for finding me, awakening me, and taking me out of that darkness for such a long journey. It was indeed a splendid adventure.
I loved watching this firework show.
The light of the rift intensifies, gradually submerging both of you. 000's body becomes ethereal. Farewell is imminent. She looks into your eyes.
Her smile carries both hope and a hint of regret.
It's okay, I'm not afraid anymore. You've brought me so many possibilities. I'd definitely catch one of them.
Maybe in someone's dream, maybe in someone else's story, oh, or perhaps, with the power of the gods, we can create a brand new world. We will meet again.
In these last moments, let me show you the road ahead.
It's alright. No matter what's ahead, and whether or not you remember later on... you've created a miracle today.
So in the future, no matter how dark the night... you will always find a way out of it.
(Scene change)
[Watch spoiler video] Montage about the future
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...It seems this is the bottom line of the world. For all the havoc these two have wrought, things just roll back to the starting point...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: How very gentle.
The time in both worlds rewinds simultaneously. Invisible hands slowly patch up the anomalous tears. Everything will eventually return to normal, for each world's system is alluringly robust.
Although 000's birth was a complete accident, it also proved that the Mania web can already cross world boundaries and reach another consciousness. This was a great surprise.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Poor Chief. He worked so hard, but brought back nothing in the end.
steps.female_content: Poor Chief. She worked so hard, but brought back nothing in the end.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...Humph, what am I talking about? It's the same for me... With this rewind, these past few days of work are all for nothing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I don't believe in gods from another dimension creating the world, nor that some file can determine one's fate or soul.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The only one who can alter 000 is her creator, but that's definitely not some gods. What invaded her was the Mania data that first contaminated her... the data you released.
steps.female_content: The only one who can alter 000 is her creator, but that's definitely not some god. What invaded her was the Mania data that first contaminated her... the data you released.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You invaded 000's core and used her belief in determinism to drive her to a dead end.
[Apply Shackles]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I won't question your methods. But in the past few days, you've secretly stolen a lot of intelligence through 000's invasion path, and you didn't report any of it, right?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The 9th Agency is right outside. They will get to the bottom of your connections with the DisCity dark web and the Underground. But for now, take me to the depths of the network, to the place where that Sinner was first contaminated.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know you remember where it is, expert.
Moore walks into the Blue Rain, conveniently washing away the bloodstains on her impressively waterproof coat.
"It's been a long time since she last killed some of those little spiders. She's getting a bit rusty, and now her favorite coat is dirty.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Sigh... I wanted to show you all the fates, settings, and files I copied, but your brother ruined everything. In a little while, I might forget everything, too.
steps.female_content: Sigh... I wanted to show you all the fates, settings, and files I copied, but your sister ruined everything. In a little while, I might forget everything, too.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oh well, it's nothing to be sorry about. If I forget, then so be it.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: The DisCity dark web operation has been completed. No need to be the scapegoat or decoy anymore. Is my job done? A long vacation wouldn't be too much to ask, right?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: After all, from what I've seen, fate will be on your side for quite some time.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oh, sorry, I almost forgot.
[CG - Return to the Underground]

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I am also your partner.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Thus, such fate is the best.
[CG - Moore takes off her hat]

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It will stand on our side.
ed
Teams Chat

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Pssst. Chief! Over here!

steps.speaker: Labyrinth
steps.content: Please forget about it. The recent game order has already used up all the budget. Please ask for money from Mess.
Strolling down the broad avenue with the Sinners, you feel no threat of danger or conspiracy. The laughter of your companions is bright and carefree. Such long-awaited ease is indeed precious.
The crowd bustles around you, basking in the summer sun. Everything is so peaceful, but you suddenly stop in your tracks.

steps.speaker: Distant Voice
steps.content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale!

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Chief, what's wrong?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Seems like I was hearing things.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Come, let's head back to the Bureau.
